newsitem.title: USA: Applied Magnetics stock tumbles on brokerage view.
newsitem.headline: Applied Magnetics stock tumbles on brokerage view.

text.p: Applied Magnetics Corp. stock tumbled in hectic trading on Thursday after the Montgomery Securities brokerage lowered its fiscal 1997 revenue estimate for the maker of computer disk drive heads.

The stock fell $5 to $33.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the most active stocks on volume of almost 2.5 million shares, nearly double its average daily volume. Less than a month ago, the stock traded at $60.50.

Paul Fox, the Montgomery analyst who cut the revenue forecast, said in an interview that he cut the revenue forecast for the year ending in September to $577 million from $616 million because Applied has a shortage of certain disk-drive head parts.
Fox continued to recommend buying Applied stock and did not lower his earnings estimates for the company.
Applied, he said, is forecast to earn $3.79 per share in the current fiscal year and $5.70 a share in fiscal 1998 next year.
The company earned $31.9 million, or $1.30 a share, on sales of $121.6 million in the first quarter ended Dec. 28.
Applied stock's sharp drop extended a substantial decline that began with the company's Feb. 24 announcement of a hostile takeover bid for Read-Rite Corp.
When it was announced, the offer to swap 0.679 Applied shares for each Read-Rite share was worth $1.8 billion.
But that total was calculated on an Applied share price of $55.25 as of the Feb. 21 market close.
The three-week tumble has wiped out a spectacular rise in Applied stock over the first six weeks of 1997.
Read-Rite, also a maker of disk drive components, said a combination with Applied would interfere with its strategy for the future and has turned down the bid.
